title: Smallpox in human history
summary: Smallpox, caused by the variola virus, was one of the greatest infectious killers of humankind and dates back at least 3,000 years. The earliest material evidence is the mummy of Pharaoh Ramses V, who died in 1157 BCE. Variolation was an early method of control, and vaccination began in 1796 with Edward Jenner. The last natural case was in 1977, and the world was declared free of it in 1980.

uncertainty.note: Initial physical evidence dates to the death of Pharaoh Ramses V (c. 1157 BCE); the global eradication of smallpox was declared by the World Health Assembly in May 1980.

as_recorded.value: The earliest material evidence for smallpox as a disease is the mummy of pharaoh Ramses V who died 1157 before common era (BCE)
The finding of smallpox-like rashes on Egyptian mummies suggests that smallpox has existed for at least 3,000 years

importance.justification: Smallpox was one of the deadliest infectious diseases in human history, shaping demographics, imperial conquests, and the development of immunization until its global eradication.
